([`concurrency/the-park-route-is-chosen-once`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-the-park-route-is-chosen-once))
- **A `push` on the queue's connection commits with the write that caused it, or neither happens** — `Core\Queue::push` on the queue's own connection enlists in whatever transaction that connection already has open. ([`concurrency/enqueue-commits-with-your-write`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-enqueue-commits-with-your-write))
- **`Core\Queue` is four members, and each is asked about a job or about a queue, never about a row number** — `Core\Queue` is `push`, `status`, `cancel` and `stats`, and nothing else. ([`concurrency/queue-four-members`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-queue-four-members))
- **A job between attempts is `Pending`, and there is no `Failed` state to ask about** — `Queue\State` is `Pending`, `Claimed`, `Succeeded`, `Dead` and `Cancelled`. ([`concurrency/a-job-between-attempts-is-pending`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-job-between-attempts-is-pending))
- **`cancel` answers whether it won the race, and it changes the job's state rather than deleting the row** — `cancel` answers a `bool`, and the `bool` says whether *this* call is what took the job out of the queue. ([`concurrency/cancel-is-a-race-it-can-lose`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-cancel-is-a-race-it-can-lose))
- **A job names a script file, and its payload crosses as a copied value** — A job names a script file — not a class, not a closure, not a static method. ([`concurrency/a-job-names-a-file`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-job-names-a-file))
- **A job's budget and grants are recorded when it is enqueued, and narrowed from that context rather than widened** *(designed)* — `push` takes the job's `limits` — the memory, CPU and time its isolate may spend — and its `grants`, and both are recorded with the row. ([`concurrency/a-jobs-budget-and-grants-are-recorded-at-enqueue`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-jobs-budget-and-grants-are-recorded-at-enqueue))
- **A worker claims a job with one statement the database arbitrates, so a fleet needs no lease protocol** — A worker claims a job with a single statement that selects the oldest due job in its queues and marks it in the same moment: `for update skip locked` on PostgreSQL and MySQL, `readpast` on SQL Server, and an immediate t… ([`concurrency/claiming-is-one-statement`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-claiming-is-one-statement))
- **Delivery is at-least-once, and idempotency is the job's own obligation** — A job may run twice, and that is stated rather than implied. ([`concurrency/delivery-is-at-least-once`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-delivery-is-at-least-once))
- **Attempts are finite, backoff is exponential and jittered, and an exhausted job is kept rather than discarded** — A job's attempts are finite with nothing configured, because an unbounded retry is an unbounded wait wearing a different name. ([`concurrency/attempts-are-finite-and-a-dead-letter-is-kept`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-attempts-are-finite-and-a-dead-letter-is-kept))
- **A job that exceeds its budget is a failed attempt, reported as that and retried like any other** — A job that exceeds its memory, CPU or time budget has had a **failed attempt**. ([`concurrency/a-budget-overrun-is-a-failed-attempt`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-budget-overrun-is-a-failed-attempt))
- **A job runs as a root isolate, and there is no second execution path** — A job runs as a **root isolate**: its own arena, its own budget, its own grants, sharing only compiled code. ([`concurrency/a-job-runs-as-a-root-isolate`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-job-runs-as-a-root-isolate))
- **Which process runs a job is configuration, and every spelling drives the identical isolate** *(designed)* — Whether jobs run inside the server process or in a worker of their own is configuration, not a different mechanism. ([`concurrency/who-runs-a-job-is-configuration`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-who-runs-a-job-is-configuration))
- **A durable payload refuses `secret`, and a `tainted` value comes back `tainted`** *(designed)* — A durable row is an output, and an output refuses `secret` (`security/secret-qualifier`). ([`concurrency/a-payload-refuses-secret-and-keeps-its-qualifiers`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-payload-refuses-secret-and-keeps-its-qualifiers))
- **A `push` on a connection other than the queue's is not transactional, and is counted rather than assumed away** *(designed)* — A `push` issued while a transaction is open on a *different* connection than the queue's is not transactional. ([`concurrency/foreign-connection-enqueue-is-counted`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-foreign-connection-enqueue-is-counted))
- **Queued work is durable, retried and declared by the application; scheduled work is a clock tick and none of those** — Two things run outside a request, and they are not variants of one mechanism. ([`concurrency/queued-work-is-not-scheduled-work`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-queued-work-is-not-scheduled-work))
- **There is no broker backend and no pluggable driver, because a driver makes transactional enqueue optional** — There is no Redis, NATS, SQS or AMQP backend, and no pluggable driver interface. ([`concurrency/no-broker-and-no-driver-interface`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-no-broker-and-no-driver-interface))
- **The reactor reports readiness on every platform, Windows included, so a stream is written once** — The reactor reports **readiness**, never completion, on every platform: epoll on Linux, kqueue on the BSDs and macOS, and on Windows a poll of `\Device\Afd` through the completion port, which turns it into a readiness s… ([`concurrency/the-reactor-reports-readiness`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-the-reactor-reports-readiness))
- **A task registers before it suspends, treats a wake as a hint, and leaves the reactor holding nothing when it ends** — Five rules govern a task that waits on I/O, and the first two are ordering rules a reader will otherwise get backwards. ([`concurrency/the-parking-contract`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-the-parking-contract))
- **A stream issues the syscall first and parks only on `WouldBlock`, so a warm socket pays nothing** — A read is: issue the syscall; on success return; on `WouldBlock` register, suspend, and loop. ([`concurrency/try-the-syscall-then-park`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-try-the-syscall-then-park))
- **A parking stream is a plain `Read` and `Write`, so nothing up the call chain is coloured** — A parking socket implements nothing but `std::io::Read` and `std::io::Write`. ([`concurrency/a-stream-is-an-ordinary-io-stream`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-stream-is-an-ordinary-io-stream))
- **A task's stack is 1 MiB of reserved address space, resident only where it is touched, and pooled per worker** — A task's stack is 1 MiB of **reserved** address space with a guard page. ([`concurrency/a-task-stack-is-reserved-wide-and-pooled`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-task-stack-is-reserved-wide-and-pooled))
- **A task's recursion limit is armed from the real bounds of the stack it was handed** — A task's recursion limit is armed from the base and length of the stack it was actually handed, not asserted from a compiled-in ceiling. ([`concurrency/a-tasks-recursion-limit-comes-from-its-own-stack`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-tasks-recursion-limit-comes-from-its-own-stack))
